exam_guide_revision: Practical Python data-stack curriculum reviewed against current official NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, and Seaborn documentation on 2026-09-19.

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; retrieval questions and typed coding questions provide the scored signal.

authoring_notes: Interactive first-pass learning for pandas. Emphasizes task-first API choice, visible DataFrame/result mental models, individual API mastery before long method-chain composition, and exact cloze reveals.

modules.title: Select, clean, and order DataFrame rows

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `loc` selects by labels or boolean conditions; `iloc` selects by integer __________.

reveal.text: `loc` selects by labels or boolean conditions; `iloc` selects by integer positions.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use `query` when a readable string expression is convenient for filtering __________.

reveal.text: Use `query` when a readable string expression is convenient for filtering rows.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Select rows with sales > 100 and only team/sales using `df.__________[mask, ["team", "sales"]]`.

reveal.text: Select rows with sales > 100 and only team/sales using `df.loc[mask, ["team", "sales"]]`.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `fillna` replaces missing values; `dropna` __________ rows or columns containing them.

reveal.text: `fillna` replaces missing values; `dropna` removes rows or columns containing them.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Fill when a defensible replacement exists; drop when the missing observation should be __________ from the analysis.

reveal.text: Fill when a defensible replacement exists; drop when the missing observation should be excluded from the analysis.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Do not fill automatically: the replacement should match the variable's meaning and the analysis __________.

reveal.text: Do not fill automatically: the replacement should match the variable's meaning and the analysis goal.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `sort_values` orders rows using one or more __________ values.

reveal.text: `sort_values` orders rows using one or more column values.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Highest sales first uses `df.sort_values("sales", ascending=__________)`.

reveal.text: Highest sales first uses `df.sort_values("sales", ascending=False)`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: `sort_index` orders by index labels; it is not the same as sorting by a data __________.

reveal.text: `sort_index` orders by index labels; it is not the same as sorting by a data column.

modules.title: Group, aggregate, transform, and compose summaries

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `groupby` partitions rows into groups based on one or more __________.

reveal.text: `groupby` partitions rows into groups based on one or more keys.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Think `split → __________ → combine`: define groups first, then compute something inside each group.

reveal.text: Think `split → apply → combine`: define groups first, then compute something inside each group.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Average sales per team starts with `df.__________("team")["sales"]...`.

reveal.text: Average sales per team starts with `df.groupby("team")["sales"]...`.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: A grouped reduction returns fewer rows: usually one summary per __________.

reveal.text: A grouped reduction returns fewer rows: usually one summary per group.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use `agg` when one grouped operation should compute __________ named summaries.

reveal.text: Use `agg` when one grouped operation should compute multiple named summaries.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Named aggregation can look like `grouped.agg(avg_sales=("sales", "__________"))`.

reveal.text: Named aggregation can look like `grouped.agg(avg_sales=("sales", "mean"))`.

nodes.title: `transform` returns values aligned to original rows

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `transform` computes within groups but returns output aligned to the original row __________.

reveal.text: `transform` computes within groups but returns output aligned to the original row index.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use `transform` when each original row needs its group's statistic, such as a team __________.

reveal.text: Use `transform` when each original row needs its group's statistic, such as a team average.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: `agg` reduces groups; `transform` preserves the original number of __________.

reveal.text: `agg` reduces groups; `transform` preserves the original number of rows.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: A grouped summary pipeline often follows `__________ → agg → sort_values`.

reveal.text: A grouped summary pipeline often follows `groupby → agg → sort_values`.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Compose these APIs only after the grouping, summary columns, and final ordering are all specified by the __________.

reveal.text: Compose these APIs only after the grouping, summary columns, and final ordering are all specified by the goal.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Do not start with a long chain if you cannot explain what intermediate __________ each step should produce.

reveal.text: Do not start with a long chain if you cannot explain what intermediate result each step should produce.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `merge` combines DataFrames by matching one or more key __________.

reveal.text: `merge` combines DataFrames by matching one or more key columns.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use a left join when every row from the __________ DataFrame must remain even without a match.

reveal.text: Use a left join when every row from the left DataFrame must remain even without a match.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: An inner join keeps only keys present on __________ sides.

reveal.text: An inner join keeps only keys present on both sides.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `pivot_table` places one field on rows, another on columns, and __________ a value field.

reveal.text: `pivot_table` places one field on rows, another on columns, and aggregates a value field.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use it for spreadsheet-like summaries such as team × month with total __________ in each cell.

reveal.text: Use it for spreadsheet-like summaries such as team × month with total sales in each cell.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: `pivot_table` can aggregate duplicates; plain `pivot` expects each index/column pair to be __________.

reveal.text: `pivot_table` can aggregate duplicates; plain `pivot` expects each index/column pair to be unique.

nodes.title: `melt` converts wide columns to long rows

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `melt` turns multiple value columns into a variable column plus a __________ column.

reveal.text: `melt` turns multiple value columns into a variable column plus a value column.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use it when columns such as Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 should become values in a single `__________` field.

reveal.text: Use it when columns such as Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 should become values in a single `quarter` field.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: `pivot_table` tends toward __________ data; `melt` tends toward long/tidy data.

reveal.text: `pivot_table` tends toward wide data; `melt` tends toward long/tidy data.
